planting.note: Plant container-grown corms or divisions in fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, sited where they will stay naturally dry through summer dormancy.

directions: Plant divisions in fall in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly alkaline soil in partial to full shade, keeping the planting site dry over the summer dormant period. Pewter Group selections of winter cyclamen were raised by Ashwood Nurseries in England by repeatedly selecting the most heavily silvered seedlings out of normal Cyclamen coum sowings, so that nearly every leaf in the strain carries a strong overall silver-gray or pewter wash rather than the typical species' marbled green-and-silver pattern. Flowers remain the usual swept-back shell-pink to carmine of the species and appear from midwinter into early spring just as the silvered foliage is at its best. Because it is a selected seed strain rather than a single clone, individual plants vary somewhat in exactly how much green edging remains around the pewter center.

planting.note: Plant divisions or potted corms in fall in sharply drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this is a clonal selection best propagated by division rather than from seed to keep its distinctive leaf and flower coloring true.

directions: Plant divisions in fall in sharply drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping the site dry through summer dormancy. 'Tilebarn Elizabeth' carries leaves that are almost entirely pewter-silver with no contrasting green veining, among the most uniformly silvered of all the named winter cyclamen selections, and in February and March it produces small bicolor flowers that are pale pink to nearly white at the base and deepen to a brighter rose-pink along the petal edges. It was selected and named by Peter Moore of Tile Barn Nursery in Kent, England, for his wife, and is one of a handful of Tilebarn-strain cyclamen selections prized by collectors for combining strong leaf silvering with distinctive two-tone flower color.

planting.note: Plant dormant tubers or potted plants in late summer to early fall, flat side up, in sharply drained soil under deciduous trees in shade to part shade, where they will stay naturally dry through summer dormancy.

directions: Plant tubers in late summer in sharply drained, humus-rich soil under deciduous trees in shade to part shade; this is a selected strain developed from the silver-leaved 'Apollo' lines of autumn cyclamen by UK specialist Phil Cornish in Gloucestershire. Its leaves emerge almost completely overlaid in solid silver-pewter, with little to none of the typical species' dark green marbling showing through, making it one of the most strikingly monochrome-silvered autumn cyclamen available. White to pale pink swept-back flowers appear from bare ground in September and October just ahead of the foliage, and the silvered leaves then persist as a dramatic ground-level carpet through winter and into spring before the plant goes dormant for summer.

planting.note: Plant dormant tubers or potted plants in late summer to early fall, flat side up, in sharply drained soil under deciduous trees in shade to part shade, where they will stay naturally dry through summer dormancy.

directions: Plant tubers in late summer in sharply drained, humus-rich soil under deciduous trees in shade to part shade; selected by UK bulb specialists Potterton and Martin from white-flowered, silver-leaved stock originally raised by Phil Cornish, this cultivar pairs an almost fully pewtered leaf — with only the faintest trace of green webbing visible on close inspection along a lightly toothed margin — with pure white flowers rather than the pink typical of the species, placing it in the albiflorum (white-flowered) form of autumn cyclamen. The combination of heavily silvered winter foliage and clean white autumn bloom makes it a useful contrast planting alongside pink-flowered hederifolium selections in a dry shaded bed under deciduous trees.

planting.note: Plant dormant tubers shallowly, flat side down, in gritty, well-drained soil under deciduous trees in partial shade; propagate by division or offset tubers to keep the distinctive leaf pattern true, since seedlings vary.

directions: Plant dormant tubers shallowly in gritty, well-drained soil under deciduous trees in partial shade, keeping the site dry through summer dormancy. 'Tilebarn Nicholas' is a named selection of the toothed-leaf wonder cyclamen distinguished by a dark green, Christmas-tree-shaped marking in the center of each leaf surrounded by a wide band of bright silver that is flushed pink as the leaves first unfurl in early fall, settling to silver and green by winter. Light pink, twisted-petaled flowers appear from September into early winter, often alongside the emerging foliage rather than strictly ahead of it as in most autumn cyclamen. It was selected and named by UK grower Peter Moore of Tile Barn Nursery and is among the most sought-after foliage forms of this smaller hardy cyclamen species.

planting.note: Plant divisions or potted corms in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in shade; unlike most hardy cyclamen, this evergreen species needs steady moisture year-round rather than a dry summer rest.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in shade, and keep the soil evenly moist through summer since this species never goes dormant. 'Lake Garda' is a strongly marked selection of European cyclamen traced to wild populations near Limone sul Garda on Italy's Lake Garda, with rounded leaves that carry a bold silver arrowhead zone in the center framed by only a thin green margin, a much more dramatic pattern than the softer marbling of typical seed-grown plants. Its fragrant flowers are a notably dark pink to magenta and appear over a long summer season from June into September. Because it does not require the dry dormancy of C. hederifolium or C. coum, it fits well into a shaded perennial border that receives regular irrigation all year.

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring before new growth emerges, or in early fall; like the species, 'Felicity' is winter-dormant and disappears completely below ground from midsummer through late winter, so mark the planting site.

directions: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade in early spring or early fall. 'Felicity' is one of the many hundreds of named Japanese cultivars of Primula sieboldii, selected for its two-toned flowers, which open white on the face but are heavily flushed with fuchsia-pink, while the back of each petal is a solid, deeper fuchsia — giving a striking contrast between front and reverse as the flowers nod and turn in a spring breeze. Like other sieboldii cultivars, its deeply cut, toothed petal lobes give the flowers a lacy texture quite different from the simple rounded blooms of common primrose. Flower color and form do not come true from seed, so divide established clumps after they go dormant in summer or just as new growth emerges in spring to maintain the named clone.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this white-flowered form spreads by rhizome just like the typical pink-flowered species and is best increased by division rather than seed.

directions: Plant divisions in fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. This is a pure white-flowered form of the Japanese woodland groundcover primrose, bearing clusters of clean white blooms above the same soft, velvety, rounded leaves as the typical magenta-pink species, and spreading by the same creeping rhizomes to form an expanding patch rather than staying in a tight clump. Because the species' usual bright rose-magenta can be a strong color to place among other woodland plants, this white selection offers a gentler option for combining with hosta, fern, and other shade perennials while keeping the same easy, spreading habit and rich green foliage.
